prompt: What is the single job of a board for one person?

choices.text: To report progress to a manager
To measure how fast you work, week by week, in points
To hold every idea you ever have
choices.why: A board with sixty cards is unread.

choices.text: To remember what you would otherwise forget

prompt: Which go on the board, by the lesson? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The current milestone's tasks
A bug noticed while doing something else
What was cut
The steps of the task in progress
choices.why: Those stay in your head or the commit.

prompt: You are fixing the page and notice that an unknown item number crashes the server. What does the lesson say to do?

choices.text: Write one card, then go back to what you were doing
Stop and fix it at once, whatever you were doing
Trust yourself to remember it tomorrow
choices.why: The board exists because you will not.

choices.text: Ignore it, since it is not in the milestone

prompt: Why does the lesson insist that cards have numbers?

choices.text: So they sort by priority on the board, highest number first
So a commit names the card it closes
So the board counts velocity each week
Because text files need numbered lines

prompt: Put the board's columns in order, left to right.
What is the one rule on the doing column?

choices.text: Every card must stay there a full day
Cards there must carry story points
One card at a time, and two at the very most
It is emptied every Friday, finished or not

prompt: The rule on the middle column is called a work-in-___ limit.
hint: What is between to do and done.

prompt: When does a card move to done?

choices.text: When the task has been started and looks promising
When it is mostly there, with small things left
At the end of the week, whatever its state
choices.why: Move it when its state changes.

choices.text: When it is committed and working

prompt: Something urgent arrives while a card is in doing. What does the lesson say?

choices.text: The card in doing goes back to to do, visibly
Put both in doing and switch between them
Finish the current card first, however long it takes
Delete the current card and start over later

prompt: Where do the done cards go at each milestone?

choices.text: Back to to do
Into a separate archive board
Into the README's decisions
Into the weekly note, as the shipped line

prompt: Match each team practice to what already does its job for one person.

pairs.right: Knowing what you did last week

prompt: What is the lesson's test for any practice not in it?

choices.text: Does it change what you do next?
Is it used by large companies?
Does the tool offer it for free?
Would a reviewer recognise the name?

prompt: Where does sprint vocabulary belong for a portfolio project, by the lesson?

choices.text: On the board, as labels on every card
In the README's first line
In the interview, as a decision
Nowhere, since it is never useful

prompt: On GitHub, what does "Closes #3" in a commit message do?
hint: When it reaches the default branch.

choices.text: Deletes issue 3 at once, along with its comments
choices.why: It closes, and only on the default branch.

choices.text: Closes it once merged, and links the two
Nothing, since GitHub treats it as a plain comment
Reopens issue 3 so that somebody reviews it

prompt: In the capture, how many loanbook commits close an issue?
A commit is part of the work on issue 3 but does not finish it. What should it say?

choices.text: Closes #3
Nothing about the issue
refs #3
Fixes everything

prompt: What does linking commits to issues give a portfolio? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: It shows the work was planned
It keeps the discussion in one place
It gives the history an index
It replaces the tests

prompt: A board has three cards in doing and none moved for a week. What does the lesson's reasoning say?

choices.text: Add a fourth column called blocked
Put two back in to do and finish one
Estimate each in story points
Start a fourth card to regain momentum

prompt: A reviewer reads "Add partial unique index" in the log and wants to know why. What gets them there in one click?
hint: The last line of the message.

choices.text: A Closes line naming the issue
A longer subject line
A burndown chart in the README
A label called important
